title: The Truth about Buying a business and Promissory Notes

If you're a buyer or a seller, they're a really valuable tool when you're structuring your deal. A promissory note is a promise to pay. It's a regular loan document. It is something that your lawyer drafts usually saying that I will pay you X amount with X amount of interest over this many years. There's other terms that really, really matter in there as well. But in the context of the deal itself, if you're buying a business, promissory notes are really, really valuable because they can bridge the gap between evaluations. For a lot of other reasons. If you think that your business is worth 1.2 million, the buyer thinks it's worth a million. They can offer you a million with a 200k promissory note and make that promissory note subject to certain conditions. If they make enough money off your business after closing in the first couple of years, turns out you were right. Your business was worth that amount. Great. They pay the note. If not, the note gets reduced. That's usually called a retention adjustment. It's a really nice way of saying, on the seller, you're the buyer. We both hope that you're right and your business is worth more. In the past, the case, I'll tell you more, but I'm not going to promise it because I'm more conservative on the buyer. description:
When buying a business, promissory notes can be a game-changer—but they can also be a huge headache if handled poorly. In this video, we dive deep into promissory seller notes, explaining what they are, how they work, and the common mistakes buyers make when using them. From vague payment terms to unrealistic interest rates, these missteps can jeopardize your deal or leave you stuck with unfavorable terms.

We’ll break down how to structure a seller note that works in your favor, the key elements to include, and how to negotiate terms that protect you in the long run. If you're buying a business with seller financing, this video will give you the tools to avoid costly mistakes and ensure the note works as a powerful asset, not a liability.

For more information on Deal Academy, a program that teaches you how to buy and sell accounting practices, click the link here:
https://www.dealacademy.org

✅To connect with Sara Sharp on LinkedIn:
https://www.linkedin.com/in/sara-sharp-9a2a98b/

✅For more information on our Mergers and Acquisitions law practice click here:
https://www.skandslegal.com
